raw_segments.text: My strength is quite failing me," I said in a soliloquy.
"'I feel I cannot go much farther. Shall I be an outcast again this night? While the
rain descends so, must I lay my head on the cold, drenched ground? I fear I cannot do otherwise,
for who will receive me? But it will be very dreadful with this feeling of hunger, faintness,
chill and this sense of desolation, this total prostration of hope. In all likelihood, though,
And why cannot I reconcile myself to the prospect of death? Why do I struggle to retain a valueless
life? Because I know or believe Mr. Rochester is living, and then, to die of want and cold,
is a fate to which nature cannot submit passively. Oh, Providence, sustain me a little longer.
